newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil-Steady, consolidating on firm demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil-Steady, consolidating on firm demand.

text.p: Singapore high sulphur fuel oil prices held steady and are consolidating after its recent gains, traders said on July 3.
Two cargoes for July loading was traded at $98 and $98.50 per tonne with a local trader buying from two separate major oil firms.
In addition to the previous cargoes purchased in the past two weeks ago, the local trader has in total bought 120,000 tonnes of fuel oil.
Traders said the buyer is covering for its term commitments in the region. The buying spree coupled with reduced Mideast supplies should support levels in the near term, traders said.
A strong Mideast market has absorbed supplies and have limited any surplus cargoes from flowing to this region.
Traders said market fundamentals were recovering from the previous doldrums but many were uncertain if the current uptrend would continue as there was no extra demand emerging from the region.
The stock drawdown on residue stocks in Singapore have also boosted sentiment. Weekly fuel oil stocks were down by 1.4 million barrels to 10.788 million barrels.
Swaps were also quoted higher, with July and August swaps quotes on par at 99.00/$99.50.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
